text:
jen_marketing: hey team — quick add to the webinar checklist. we need a defensible set of benchmark numbers (hosted vs dedicated) that the comms team can quote. can runtime own a rerun + validation and drop the results into s3? :mag:

zara_marketing: specifically we want: p50/p90/p99 token latency, throughput at 10/50/200 QPS, cost per 1k tokens (current pricing assumptions), and 6 sample outputs for human check. CSV + short JSON summary please.

sam_marketing: add: clearly mark which rows are cold-cache vs warmed-cache, and include the exact hardware kernel flags + CUDA/cuDNN versions. also include region labels (us-west1, eu-west1).

lia_eng_runtime: ok. propose we standardize the methodology: - model set: amy-small.fp16, amy-base.int8, amy-large.fp16 - seq lens: 256, 512, 1024 - cache: cold (first request), warmed (after 50 warmups) - samples: 1k prompts per config (deterministic seed) - qps targets: 10/50/200 - measure: p50/p90/p99 (ms per token), tokens/sec, tokens-per-second-per-GPU, cost-per-1k (based on reserved g5 price)

noah_runtime: note on int8: run on g5.xlarge with nvllc=1 and "perf_mode=throughput". i'll include the exact boot options. for hosted runs we'll hit the hosted API gateway; for dedicated we'll direct to the dedicated pool endpoint (dedicated-pool-42). need service account for hosted auth?

jen_marketing: yes, use the marketing-bench SA. please don't publish keys in results; just note the auth method.

lia_eng_runtime: plan: 1) spin bench jobs with BENCH_ID=webinar_1772600001 2) store raw logs + histograms in s3://redwood-marketing/bench-webinar-1772600001/ 3) produce outputs: results.csv, summary.json, latency_histograms.png, top_outliers.trace 4) run a small QA script that checks for OOMs, >2x variance across repeated runs, anomalous p99 spikes.

qa_bot: automated checklist: will validate CSV headers, ensure sample count >= 900, check for NaNs, and compute simple bootstrap 95% CI for p90. failure -> flag run.

zara_marketing: timeline: can you do a smoke by EOD and the full suite by Thu noon? webinar dry-run is Fri.

lia_eng_runtime: smoke yes. will run reduced sample (100 prompts) across three models and post link. full runs are queued; estimate ~6h total wall time (parallelized across pools).

noah_runtime: run command (exact copy):
```bash
export BENCH_ID=webinar_1772600001
export S3_PREFIX=s3://redwood-marketing/bench-webinar-1772600001/$BENCH_ID
./bench_runner \
  --model $MODEL_ID \
  --quant $QUANT \
  --seq_len $SEQ \
  --qps_targets 10,50,200 \
  --samples 1000 \
  --warmups 50 \
  --out $S3_PREFIX/results.csv \
  --raw-logs $S3_PREFIX/raw.log
```

benchbot: scheduled webinar_1772600001-smoke on g5.allocated-3 at 2026-03-22T09:10:00Z

jen_marketing: one last ask: marketing needs a single headline and a fallback conservative number. please call out which number we should use for the headline (e.g., p90 at 50 QPS on hosted) and why (best replicate real traffic). and include the top-3 failure modes observed (OOM, long GC pauses, transient network spikes).

lia_eng_runtime: will annotate summary.json with "headline_recommendation": {"metric":"p90","qps":50,"env":"hosted","note":"represents interactive traffic; conservative after verifying warmed-cache"} and list failure modes.

sam_marketing: awesome. ping this thread with the s3 link to the smoke CSV when it's done and a 1-sentence summary for the deck.

lia_eng_runtime: smoke started; will post link in ~20m. full run started after smoke pass.

noah_runtime: FYI I'll also attach a tiny sample prompts pack (50 prompts) for manual QA in results/manual_checks/

zara_marketing: thanks folks! :rocket:
